sentences.text: Prestosuchus is an extinct genus of pseudosuchian belonging to the group Loricata that lived in Brazil during the Middle Triassic.
This animal possessed a deep skull and serrated teeth similar to its relatives.
The premaxilla of Prestosuchus has a tall, boxy main body containing four teeth.
The maxilla of Prestosuchus is deep and roughly textured, featuring a low triangular antorbital fenestra and 11 to 13 large teeth.
The neck vertebrae of Prestosuchus are tall and feature large ventral depressions that create a keel on their lower edge.
Prestosuchus had two-headed dorsal ribs similar to those of Batrachotomus and a dense gastral basket.
In Prestosuchus, the scapula and coracoid are strongly connected but not fused.
The ilium of Prestosuchus features a deep bony acetabulum covered by a horizontal supraacetabular crest.
A notable complete skeleton with a well-preserved hind limb was discovered in 2010 in Dona Francisca, Rio Grande do Sul, by a team from the Universidade Luterana do Brasil.
The only Prestosuchus fossil stored outside Brazil and Germany is a fragmentary specimen held at Harvard's Museum of Comparative Zoology in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
The holotype of Prestosuchus chiniquensis was discovered by Wilhelm Rau alongside the holotype of Rauisuchus tiradentes.
The holotypes were found in 1928 or 1929 within the Santa Maria Formation at the Paleontological Site Chiniquá near São Pedro do Sul, Brazil.
Prestosuchus chiniquensis was discovered in 1938 at the Chiniquá paleontological site near São Pedro do Sul by the German paleontologist Friedrich von Huene.
Von Huene named the genus Prestosuchus in honor of Vicentino Prestes de Almeida.
Prestosuchus likely walked on four legs with an upright semi-erect stance, having limb bones positioned below the hips, unlike modern crocodilians.
Prestosuchus walked on four legs like crocodilians but could maintain a semi-upright posture due to its hind limb bones being positioned under the hips.
Prestosuchus was likely an apex predator in its habitat.
Prestosuchus has historically been classified as a rauisuchian and as the defining member of the family Prestosuchidae.
The genus Prestosuchus was described by von Huene in 1942.
The type species of the genus Prestosuchus is P. chiniquensis, described by von Huene in 1942.
Researchers suggest that the leg musculature of Prestosuchus represents a primitive condition for archosaurs rather than a derived one.
The fossil range of Prestosuchus is the Middle Triassic, specifically the Ladinian stage.
Prestosuchus lived from the Ladinian to the Carnian stages, between 241.464 and 227.3 million years ago.
All undisputed fossils of Prestosuchus come from the lower Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
It is debated whether the groups Rauisuchia and Prestosuchidae are valid, as Rauisuchia is considered paraphyletic and Prestosuchidae is polyphyletic in its widest form.
There is an ongoing debate regarding the exact number of species contained within the genus Prestosuchus.
Some researchers have suggested that Procerosuchus celer and Prestosuchus loricatus are junior synonyms of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.

Researchers Kischlat and Barberena (1999) proposed that certain Prestosuchus fossils, including the paralectotype of P. chiniquensis and the Porto Alegre specimen, should be classified as a new genus and species.
Kischlat (2000) proposed the name "Karamuru vorax" for specific fossils previously referred to Prestosuchus, based on a 1999 abstract.
Some researchers consider the unique notch at the scapula-coracoid suture an autapomorphy of Prestosuchus, as it has not been reported in other loricatans.
It is debated whether "P." loricatus belongs to Prestosuchus, as it lacks several pelvic autapomorphies found in P. chiniquensis and P. nyassicus, suggesting it may be a different genus.
